claims.text: The untreated W–Cu composite contains isolated W particles or an interconnected W ligament network embedded in a Cu matrix.
The untreated W–Cu composite has poorly bonded interfaces and interfacial voids.
A single-step HIP post-treatment at high pressure and moderate temperature can overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation in the W–Cu composite.
HIP will improve bonding between the W phase and the Cu matrix.
Improved W–Cu bonding will create more continuous thermal-conduction pathways.
The proposed HIP treatment uses 0.5–1 GPa pressure, 850–950 °C, a duration of 1–2 hours, and an inert atmosphere.
The proposed HIP conditions will promote plastic deformation or flow of the Cu matrix.
The proposed HIP conditions will reduce interfacial void volume and improve W–Cu contact.
The proposed HIP conditions will avoid deleterious phase transformations.
Pressure-assisted densification and enhanced interfacial diffusion will eliminate interfacial voids and improve W–Cu interfacial bonding.
High isostatic pressure and moderate temperature enhance atomic diffusion at W–Cu interfaces.
HIP reduces local stresses that drive phase separation.
HIP minimizes the nucleation and growth of interfacial voids.
More coherent W–Cu interphase contact facilitates heat conduction across the composite.
HIP-treated samples will have measurably higher effective thermal conductivity than untreated samples under simulated heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
HIP treatment will enhance joint stability under cyclic thermal loading and irradiation.
Interfacial voids in the untreated composite interrupt heat paths and lower effective thermal conductivity.
The HIP benefit will persist only below service temperatures and irradiation doses that reinitiate void formation or cause substantial microstructural coarsening.
The treatment may be inadequate for service environments outside the proposed or tested processing and service envelope.
